issues.title: Unbound multilinear arity in nonlinear LTE recurrence
issues.failure_explanation: The old formula does not define Δg_0^{\{i\}} because different multilinear arities k are distinct contributions and no fixed k is in scope. Eq:dgFull establishes that all admissible arities must be summed, with the positive-composition constraint giving the finite range.
issues.overall_effect: The recursive coefficient characterization in thm:LTE is undefined as printed, so the subsequent tree representation and LTE/global-error chain lack formal support until the missing binder is supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In eq:LTE_coeffs:g, insert the missing sum over k=1,…,i−ℓ before the positive-composition sum, so that the coefficient is summed over ℓ=0,…,i−1, all admissible arities k, and positive m₁,…,m_k satisfying m₁+⋯+m_k=i−ℓ. This makes the recurrence well-defined and removes this obstruction from the recorded tree, LTE, and convergence chain without changing any statement.
issues.why_classification: Eq:dgFull already explicitly sums over the multilinear arity k, and positivity of the composition uniquely forces the finite range k≤i−ℓ. The proof therefore supplies the complete mathematics; only a syntactic binder was omitted from the displayed recurrence. No inference, guarantee, or downstream statement needs alteration.

issues.title: Missing stiff stage-defect term in third-order LTE display
issues.failure_explanation: The general recurrence contributes h^3(b^T⊗Z)(I−A⊗Z)^{-1}(γ_3⊗y^{(3)}(t_0)) at order three. The old specialization contains the other order-three contributions but not this one, so the labeled expansion is incomplete.
issues.overall_effect: Only the illustrative third-order specialization is incorrect; the preceding general LTE lemma already contains the required contribution and no later formal result depends on this display.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the order-h³ summand h³(bᵀ⊗Z)(I−A⊗Z)⁻¹(γ₃⊗y⁽³⁾(t₀)) to eq:LTE_order_3, leaving the other terms and the O(h⁴) remainder unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The i=3 instance of eq:LTE_coeffs:y uniquely supplies this exact summand. The omission is confined to an illustrative specialization, and no later formal result uses the display. Inserting the source-forced term is therefore transcriptional and requires no repair to an argument or guarantee.

issues.title: Off-by-one indexing in abstract tree induction and LTE instantiation
issues.failure_explanation: The induction does not substitute the recurrence it is proving: its direct term must be α_i and corresponds to the pure bushy tree [τ_0^i], which has i+1 vertices. Using α_{i+1} invalidates that induction step and induces the corresponding one-order mismatch in the later output-LTE application.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract representation lemma is not proved with the stated recurrence, and the same indexing mismatch obstructs its application to the output LTE; consequently the tree representation and results relying on it are not established as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the induction proof of lem:abstractrec, use the direct term α_i in the formula for v_{i+1} and identify it with the pure bushy tree [τ₀^i]. Reindex the output-LTE instantiation correspondingly, so that α_i contains the order-(i+1) direct forcing terms involving γ_{i+1}, γ̂_{i+1}, and y⁽ⁱ⁺¹⁾. With these coordinated index corrections, the abstract lemma applies to the output recurrence and this indexing obstruction is removed from thm:LTE_trees and its recorded consumers.
issues.why_classification: The proof literally substitutes the wrong forcing index and the output application repeats the resulting order mismatch, so this is more than a transcriptional typo. Nevertheless, the stated recurrence and tree vertex count uniquely determine a short, routine reindexing; no new lemma, proof architecture, weakened statement, rate, or guarantee is required.

issues.title: Extraneous A factor in output tree-map instantiation
issues.failure_explanation: The A factor belongs to the stage-error recursion, where Δg is first multiplied by A. It does not occur in the step/output recurrence. Consequently, the old output-map assignment does not reproduce eq:LTE_coeffs:y or the stated formula eq:LTE_tree:psi and cannot prove the output part of thm:LTE_trees.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the output LTE tree representation uses the wrong map, leaving that part of thm:LTE_trees and its LTE/global-error consumers unsupported as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the output-map instantiation in the proof of thm:LTE_trees, replace ((A C^ℓ)⊗I) by (C^ℓ⊗I), retaining the A factor only in the separate stage-error map. The corrected output map then reproduces eq:LTE_coeffs:y and eq:LTE_tree:psi, restoring this issue's support for the recorded LTE and convergence consumers.
issues.why_classification: The extra A makes the actual application of the abstract lemma invalid, so the defect is substantive rather than merely typographical. Both the output recurrence and the theorem's stated ψ-map uniquely determine the A-free correction, which is short and local and preserves every affected statement and guarantee without a new lemma or proof architecture.

issues.title: Off-by-one propagator index in global-error proof
issues.failure_explanation: Applying eq:C-stability with its step index replaced by n−1 gives (R(Z)+hΛ_{n−1})Δy_{n−1}. The old Eq:ErrRecursion therefore does not literally follow from the invoked lemma with the established Λ-indexing.
issues.overall_effect: The propagation identity in the convergence proof is misindexed, although the subsequent estimates require only the same uniform bound on Λ and are unchanged after consistent reindexing.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply eq:C-stability at step n−1 and use Λ_{n−1}, rather than Λ_n, in Eq:ErrRecursion and in the corresponding propagator and hΛξ term of the shifted-error recurrence. Keep all subsequent estimates unchanged, since they use only the same uniform bound on Λ.
issues.why_classification: The step from n−1 to n uniquely fixes the index as n−1. The proof never uses any index-specific property of Λ, only its uniform norm bound, so consistent relabeling changes no inference, estimate, convergence rate, or theorem scope. This is a transcriptional off-by-one index slip.
